guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / panic attack and grounding
title: Panic attack at a royal event
setting: Crowded royal event. 17M student has severe anxiety, panicked breathing, disoriented, struggling to focus on words, trying to run away.
verdictExplanation: Anxiety mimic of systemic issues, requires full diagnostic check, calm grounding, and airway management. Sick: manage and monitor closely.

history.history: Struggled with the vast amount of people around him at a royal event, became disoriented

followUp.question: What is the appropriate first aid management for this panicked patient?

options.text: Escort him away from the crowd to a quiet area, encourage slow breathing, and ground him using calming reassurance
Force him to breathe into a paper bag to stop hyperventilation
Call 999 for a priority emergency response immediately
Give him a cold glass of water and tell him to ignore the crowd

followUp.explanation: Panic attacks are managed by moving the patient away from the trigger (crowds), encouraging slow controlled breathing, and grounding them with calm, clear reassurance. Paper bags are no longer recommended due to hypoxia risks. 999 is only needed if systemic issues develop.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Move to a quiet area, encourage slow breathing. Reassure and ground the patient.
levelFlags.erNotes: Ground the patient, check BGL to rule out hypoglycaemia (mimics anxiety), monitor SpO₂ and BP. Escort away from the crowd with stewards.
